questions.question: A hypervisor is:

options.B: Software that creates, runs and manages virtual machines

questions.explanation: A hypervisor is software that creates, runs and manages virtual machines.

questions.question: In a virtual environment, many VMs share:
questions.explanation: Virtualization lets many VMs run on, and share, the same physical hardware.

questions.question: VM escape means:

options.A: An attacker breaks out of a VM and reaches the host system
options.B: A VM is deleted by mistake
options.C: A VM is moved to another host

questions.explanation: In a VM escape, an attacker breaks out of the VM's isolation and reaches the host system.

questions.question: A zero-day vulnerability is:

options.A: A weakness fixed on the first day
options.B: A weakness found only in old software
options.C: An unknown weakness for which no patch is available yet
options.D: A weakness that cannot be exploited

questions.explanation: A zero-day is a weakness that is not yet known to the vendor, so no patch exists yet.

questions.question: VM isolation means:

options.B: Giving all VMs the same data
options.C: Connecting every VM to every other VM
options.D: Keeping each VM separate so it cannot see or change another VM's data

questions.explanation: Isolation keeps each VM separate so that it cannot see or change the data of other VMs.

questions.question: A side-channel attack learns secrets by:

options.A: Observing how shared resources are used

questions.explanation: A side-channel attack infers secrets by observing how shared resources (such as CPU or cache) are used.

questions.question: Data at rest means data:

options.B: Stored on disks, virtual disk files and backups

questions.explanation: Data at rest is data that is stored, for example on disks, virtual disk files and backups.

questions.question: Data in transit means data:

options.C: Moving across the network, for example during VM migration

questions.explanation: Data in transit is data moving across the network, such as during VM migration.

questions.question: Encryption converts readable data into:
questions.explanation: Encryption turns readable data into an unreadable coded form that needs a key to read.

questions.question: An insider threat comes from:

options.D: A person inside the organization who misuses their access

questions.explanation: An insider threat comes from someone inside the organization who misuses their access.

questions.question: Sandboxing runs a program or VM in:
questions.explanation: Sandboxing runs a program or VM in a restricted, isolated environment so it cannot harm the rest of the system.

questions.question: VLAN stands for:
questions.explanation: VLAN stands for Virtual Local Area Network.

questions.question: Containers share the host operating system's:
questions.explanation: Containers share the host operating system's kernel instead of having their own guest OS.

questions.question: SELinux and AppArmor are used to improve the security of:
questions.explanation: SELinux and AppArmor are Linux security modules that restrict and secure containers.

questions.question: Micro-segmentation divides the network into:

options.D: Very small secure zones, down to a single VM or workload

questions.explanation: Micro-segmentation creates very small secure zones, down to a single VM or workload.

questions.question: Which tool provides micro-segmentation and firewalling in VMware?
questions.explanation: VMware NSX provides micro-segmentation and firewalling in VMware environments.

questions.question: Least privilege access means users get:

options.A: Only the permissions required for their role

questions.explanation: Least privilege gives users only the permissions required for their role.

questions.question: Separation of duties means:
questions.explanation: Separation of duties divides responsibilities among different administrators so no one person has full control.

questions.question: CIS Benchmarks are used for:
questions.explanation: CIS Benchmarks give recommended secure configurations used for hypervisor hardening.

questions.question: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS):

options.B: Detects suspicious or unauthorized activity and raises an alert

questions.explanation: An IDS detects suspicious or unauthorized activity and raises an alert.

questions.question: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) needs:

options.D: More than one proof of identity

questions.explanation: MFA requires more than one proof of identity, such as a password plus a code.

questions.question: A VM template is:

options.B: A master copy used to create new VMs

questions.explanation: A VM template is a master copy used to create new VMs.

questions.question: Logging is:

options.A: The recording of events and activities such as logins and VM creation

questions.explanation: Logging records events and activities such as logins and VM creation.

questions.question: Qualys VMDR is used to:

options.C: Scan for vulnerabilities in virtual environments

questions.explanation: Qualys VMDR scans virtual environments for vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Tripwire Enterprise detects:
questions.explanation: Tripwire Enterprise detects unauthorized changes to configurations.

questions.question: CrowdStrike offers:
questions.explanation: CrowdStrike offers endpoint security for virtualized systems.

questions.question: Microsoft Defender for Cloud protects workloads running on:
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud protects workloads running on Microsoft Hyper-V.

questions.question: The key performance metrics (C-M-D-N-H) are:

options.C: CPU, Memory, Disk I/O, Network, Hypervisor

questions.explanation: C-M-D-N-H stands for CPU, Memory, Disk I/O, Network and Hypervisor.

questions.question: Memory ballooning is used to:

options.A: Reclaim unused memory from a VM for other VMs

questions.explanation: Memory ballooning reclaims unused memory from one VM so other VMs can use it.

questions.question: Resource over-commitment means:

options.A: Giving VMs fewer resources than needed
options.B: Giving VMs exactly what the host has
options.D: Allocating more resources to VMs than the host actually has

questions.explanation: Over-commitment allocates more resources to VMs than the host physically has.

questions.question: A reservation is:

options.A: The maximum amount of a resource
options.C: The minimum amount of a resource guaranteed to a VM

questions.explanation: A reservation is the minimum amount of a resource guaranteed to a VM.

questions.question: A limit is:

options.B: The maximum amount of a resource a VM can use

questions.explanation: A limit is the maximum amount of a resource a VM can use.

questions.question: Shares decide:

options.C: The priority of a VM when resources are short

questions.explanation: Shares decide a VM's priority when resources are short.

questions.question: Thin provisioning allocates storage:

options.A: On demand, when data is actually written

questions.explanation: Thin provisioning allocates storage on demand, only when data is actually written.

questions.question: Deduplication means:

options.B: Removing duplicate copies of data and keeping only one

questions.explanation: Deduplication removes duplicate copies of data and keeps only one.

questions.question: Caching means:

options.D: Keeping frequently used data in fast memory or fast storage

questions.explanation: Caching keeps frequently used data in fast memory or fast storage for quicker access.

questions.question: Jumbo frames are Ethernet frames up to about:
questions.explanation: Jumbo frames are larger than the standard 1500 bytes and go up to about 9000 bytes.

questions.question: SDN manages the network through:
questions.explanation: Software Defined Networking (SDN) manages the network through software.

questions.question: Right-sizing means giving each VM:

options.A: Exactly the resources its workload needs

questions.explanation: Right-sizing gives each VM exactly the resources its workload needs.

questions.question: A snapshot saves:

options.C: The state of a VM at a particular time

questions.explanation: A snapshot saves the state of a VM at a particular point in time.

questions.question: Load balancing means:

options.A: Putting all work on one host
options.D: Distributing workloads evenly across available resources

questions.explanation: Load balancing distributes workloads evenly across the available resources.

questions.question: vSphere DRS stands for:
questions.explanation: DRS stands for Distributed Resource Scheduler.

questions.question: High availability (HA) aims for:

options.A: Minimum downtime even if hardware or software fails

questions.explanation: HA aims for minimum downtime even when hardware or software fails.

questions.question: The name of live migration in VMware is:
questions.explanation: In VMware, live migration is called vMotion.

questions.question: The name of live migration in Hyper-V is:
questions.explanation: In Hyper-V, live migration is simply called Live Migration.

questions.question: ESXi is:
questions.explanation: ESXi is the VMware hypervisor.

questions.question: vCenter is the:

options.C: Central management tool of VMware vSphere

questions.explanation: vCenter is the central management tool of VMware vSphere.

questions.question: KVM is:

options.D: An open-source virtualization solution for Linux

questions.explanation: KVM is an open-source virtualization solution for Linux.

questions.question: Xen is widely used in cloud environments such as:
questions.explanation: Xen is widely used in cloud environments such as AWS.

questions.question: Microsoft Hyper-V is the native hypervisor in:
questions.explanation: Hyper-V is Microsoft's native hypervisor built into Windows Server.

questions.question: Why is a hypervisor compromise so serious?

options.A: It can affect all the VMs hosted on it
options.C: It affects only the network cable
options.D: It affects only the user's browser

questions.explanation: The hypervisor controls all the VMs on the host, so compromising it can affect all of them.

questions.question: A weakness in a test VM should never give access to a bank VM on the same host. Which security aim is this?
questions.explanation: Keeping one VM's weakness from reaching another VM on the same host is the goal of isolation.

questions.question: Which is a challenge of dynamic environments?

options.D: It is difficult to track, secure and audit VMs that keep moving and changing

questions.explanation: In dynamic environments VMs keep moving and changing, which makes them hard to track, secure and audit.

questions.question: Data may be exposed during VM migration if it is not:
questions.explanation: Data in transit during migration can be exposed if it is not encrypted.

questions.question: Which two practices together reduce the risk from insider threats?

options.A: Least privilege and separation of duties

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits what each person can do, and separation of duties prevents one person having complete control; together they reduce insider risk.

questions.question: Which is NOT a technique used for VM isolation?
questions.explanation: Thin provisioning is a storage technique; sandboxing, VLANs and firewalls are isolation techniques.

questions.question: A major benefit of network segmentation is that:

options.A: All VMs can talk to each other
options.C: An attack is limited to one part of the network

questions.explanation: Segmentation limits an attack to one part of the network.

questions.question: Container isolation is generally weaker than VM isolation because containers:
questions.explanation: Containers share the host kernel, so isolation is weaker than for VMs, which each have their own guest OS.

questions.question: Micro-segmentation mainly stops:

options.D: Lateral (sideways) movement of attackers between VMs

questions.explanation: Micro-segmentation mainly stops attackers from moving sideways between VMs.

questions.question: Hypervisor hardening includes:

options.A: Regular patches, disabling unused services, limiting admin access and following CIS Benchmarks

questions.explanation: Hardening includes regular patches, disabling unused services, limiting admin access and following CIS Benchmarks.

questions.question: Why must both the hypervisor and the VMs be monitored?

options.B: Monitoring only one of them misses attacks at the other level
options.C: Only the hypervisor can be attacked

questions.explanation: Attacks can happen at both levels, so monitoring only one would miss attacks at the other.

questions.question: Why are secure VM templates important?

options.C: Every new VM created from the template inherits its strengths or weaknesses
options.D: They remove the need for patching

questions.explanation: Every VM created from a template inherits its strengths or weaknesses, so the template must be secure.

questions.question: Auditing is best described as:

options.A: Reviewing logs to confirm rules are followed and to find problems

questions.explanation: Auditing reviews logs to confirm rules are followed and to find problems.

questions.question: Which tool detects unauthorized changes to configurations?
questions.explanation: Tripwire Enterprise detects unauthorized changes to configurations.

questions.question: Memory ballooning works with the help of:

options.B: A balloon driver installed inside the guest VM

questions.explanation: Ballooning relies on a balloon driver installed inside the guest VM.

questions.question: Scheduler latency is:

options.A: The time taken to write to disk
options.B: The time taken to boot a VM
options.C: The time a VM waits for its turn on the physical CPU
options.D: The time taken to encrypt data

questions.explanation: Scheduler latency is the time a VM waits for its turn on the physical CPU.

questions.question: High VM swap activity shows:
questions.explanation: High swap activity means physical memory is short, so VM memory is being moved to disk.

questions.question: A host has 64 GB RAM, but VMs are given a total of 100 GB. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Allocating 100 GB to VMs on a host with 64 GB RAM is over-commitment.

questions.question: Which is a risk of excessive over-commitment?
questions.explanation: Excessive over-commitment causes resource contention and heavy swapping.

questions.question: A production VM should get priority over a test VM when resources are short. Which setting is used?
questions.explanation: Shares set a VM's priority when resources are short.

questions.question: A VM has a 100 GB virtual disk but only 20 GB of data and uses only 20 GB of physical storage. Which technique is used?
questions.explanation: Using only 20 GB of physical storage for a 100 GB virtual disk with 20 GB of data is thin provisioning.

questions.question: Deduplication is very useful in virtualization because:

options.D: Many VMs have the same operating system files

questions.explanation: Many VMs hold identical operating system files, so deduplication saves a lot of space.

questions.question: A requirement for using jumbo frames is that:

options.B: All devices in the network path must support them

questions.explanation: Every device in the network path must support jumbo frames for them to work.

questions.question: A benefit of SDN is that:

options.A: Physical devices must be replaced for each change
options.C: Network settings can be changed quickly without changing physical devices

questions.explanation: With SDN, network settings can be changed quickly through software without changing physical devices.

questions.question: Under-provisioning a VM results in:
questions.explanation: Giving a VM too few resources results in a slow VM.

questions.question: Which problem is caused by stale snapshots?

options.A: They waste storage and slow down disks

questions.explanation: Old snapshots waste storage and slow down disks.

questions.question: vSphere DRS moves VMs between hosts using:
questions.explanation: DRS uses vMotion to move running VMs between hosts.

questions.question: Which HA technique restarts the VMs of a failed host on healthy hosts?
questions.explanation: Clustered hosts allow the VMs of a failed host to be restarted on healthy hosts.

questions.question: Replication protects mainly against:
questions.explanation: Replication keeps a copy at another site, protecting mainly against site failure or disaster.

questions.question: How does live migration improve availability?

options.D: Hosts can be maintained with no downtime because VMs are moved away first

questions.explanation: VMs are moved away first, so hosts can be maintained with no downtime.

questions.question: Microsoft Hyper-V integrates with which cloud for hybrid deployments?
questions.explanation: Hyper-V integrates with Microsoft Azure for hybrid deployments.

questions.question: Xen supports:
questions.explanation: Xen supports both para-virtualization and full virtualization.

questions.question: Hyper-V Manager simplifies VM management because:

options.A: It works only by command line
options.D: It is a graphical console to create, configure and manage VMs and virtual switches

questions.explanation: Hyper-V Manager is a graphical console for creating, configuring and managing VMs and virtual switches.

questions.question: KVM turns:

options.A: The Linux kernel into a hypervisor

questions.explanation: KVM turns the Linux kernel into a hypervisor.

questions.question: An advantage of open-source hypervisors like KVM and Xen is:
questions.explanation: Open-source hypervisors like KVM and Xen have no licence cost.

questions.question: Which VMware tool provides micro-segmentation and firewalling for vSphere?
questions.explanation: NSX provides micro-segmentation and firewalling for vSphere.

questions.question: In the Hyper-V lab, which step is done after setting up the Hyper-V role?

options.A: Create VMs and configure virtual switches

questions.explanation: After setting up the Hyper-V role, the next step is to create VMs and configure virtual switches.

questions.question: In the vSphere lab, which features are tested?
questions.explanation: The vSphere lab tests vMotion, High Availability and DRS.

questions.question: What is the first general step when setting up VM replication in Hyper-V?

options.C: Prepare two Hyper-V servers: primary and replica

questions.explanation: Replication first needs two Hyper-V servers: a primary server and a replica server.

questions.question: In Hyper-V replication, "Enable Replication" is selected on the:
questions.explanation: "Enable Replication" is selected for the VM on the primary server.

questions.question: What is the scalability of Microsoft Hyper-V in the comparison table?
questions.explanation: In the comparison table, Hyper-V's scalability is Medium.

questions.question: What is the licensing of KVM?
questions.explanation: KVM is open-source.

questions.question: Which is the management interface of Xen?
questions.explanation: XenCenter is the management interface of Xen.

questions.question: xentop is a command-line monitoring tool for:
questions.explanation: xentop is a command-line monitoring tool for Xen.

questions.question: esxtop is a command-line tool on:
questions.explanation: esxtop is a command-line monitoring tool on ESXi.

questions.question: Which tool is used to monitor performance on Microsoft Hyper-V?
questions.explanation: Performance Monitor (PerfMon) is used to monitor performance on Hyper-V.

questions.question: Which tools are commonly used with KVM?
questions.explanation: virt-manager and virsh are commonly used with KVM.

questions.question: Which is a way to reduce side-channel attacks?

options.A: Placing sensitive VMs beside untrusted VMs
options.C: Avoiding placing sensitive VMs on the same host as untrusted VMs

questions.explanation: Side-channel attacks need shared hardware, so keeping sensitive VMs off hosts shared with untrusted VMs reduces the risk.

questions.question: Which is a key difference between VM isolation and container isolation?

options.A: Each VM has its own guest OS, while containers share the host kernel
options.B: VMs share the kernel, containers have own OS

questions.explanation: Each VM has its own guest OS, whereas containers share the host kernel.

questions.question: Which is an example of separation of duties?

options.A: One admin creates VMs, manages the network and reviews logs
options.B: All admins use the same account
options.D: One admin creates VMs, another manages the network, a third reviews the logs

questions.explanation: Splitting VM creation, network management and log review among three different admins is separation of duties.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates VM escape from a side-channel attack?

options.A: Both break out of the VM to reach the host
options.C: VM escape reaches the host from inside a VM, while a side-channel attack infers secrets by observing shared resource use

questions.explanation: VM escape breaks out of a VM to reach the host, while a side-channel attack only infers secrets by observing shared resource use.

questions.question: Why can patching alone NOT stop a zero-day attack on a hypervisor?

options.A: No patch exists yet for an unknown weakness, so hardening, limited admin access and monitoring are also needed
options.C: Zero-day attacks affect only guest VMs

questions.explanation: A zero-day has no patch yet, so hardening, limited admin access and monitoring are also needed.

questions.question: Which statement about container isolation is INCORRECT?

options.B: SELinux and AppArmor can restrict containers
options.C: A kernel vulnerability can become a risk for all containers
options.D: Each container has its own full guest operating system

questions.explanation: Containers do not have their own full guest OS; they share the host kernel, so this statement is incorrect.

questions.question: How does micro-segmentation differ from normal segmentation?

options.A: It uses one large zone for all VMs
options.B: It can apply separate security policies down to a single VM or workload
options.D: It works only on physical servers

questions.explanation: Micro-segmentation can apply separate security policies down to a single VM or workload.

questions.question: Which feature allows security rules to follow a VM when it moves to another host?
questions.explanation: Micro-segmentation policies are tied to the VM or workload, so they follow it when it moves.

questions.question: Which tool-purpose pair is WRONG?

options.C: Tripwire Enterprise – detecting unauthorized configuration changes
options.D: CrowdStrike – protecting Hyper-V workloads as its main role

questions.explanation: CrowdStrike's role is endpoint security for virtualized systems, and protecting Hyper-V workloads is the role of Microsoft Defender for Cloud, so this pair is wrong.

questions.question: Why is IDS at the hypervisor/platform level important?

options.A: Traffic between VMs on the same host is not visible to traditional physical network tools
options.C: Physical firewalls see all VM-to-VM traffic

questions.explanation: Traffic between VMs on the same host does not leave the host, so traditional physical network tools cannot see it.

questions.question: Which statement about monitoring is correct?

options.A: An attack on a VM affects all VMs on the host
options.B: An attack on the hypervisor affects all VMs, while an attack on a VM affects only that VM and its data

questions.explanation: A hypervisor attack can affect all VMs, while a VM attack affects only that VM and its data, so both levels need monitoring.

questions.question: A VM template has an unpatched weakness. What is the result?

options.D: Every VM created from it will also have that weakness

questions.explanation: Every VM created from the template inherits its weakness.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the security best practices (E-A-P-L-S) listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: Over-committing resources is a performance topic, not one of the E-A-P-L-S security best practices.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares least privilege and separation of duties?

options.A: Both give every admin full rights
options.B: Least privilege limits rights to the role's needs; separation of duties divides work so no one person has complete control
options.C: Least privilege divides tasks; separation of duties limits rights

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits rights to what a role needs, while separation of duties divides work so no one person has complete control.

questions.question: CPU usage looks normal, but applications feel slow. Which metric may reveal hidden delays?
questions.explanation: Scheduler latency shows how long VMs wait for the physical CPU, which can cause slowness even when CPU usage looks normal.

questions.question: Why might VM swap activity suddenly increase?

options.C: Physical memory is short, so the hypervisor moves VM memory to disk

questions.explanation: When physical memory is short, the hypervisor moves VM memory to disk, which increases swap activity.

questions.question: Which statement about memory ballooning is correct?

options.A: The balloon driver is installed on the physical switch
options.B: The balloon inflates only when memory is plentiful
options.D: The balloon inflates when the host is short of memory and deflates when memory is available again

questions.explanation: The balloon inflates to reclaim memory when the host is short and deflates when memory is available again.

questions.question: Which caution applies to thin provisioning?

options.A: The administrator must monitor storage so that it does not become full
options.C: It allocates full space at the start

questions.explanation: Because thin provisioning allocates space on demand, storage must be monitored so it does not run out.

questions.question: "A test VM cannot use more than 2 CPUs." This describes a:
questions.explanation: A cap on the maximum resource a VM can use is a limit.

questions.question: "A database VM always gets at least 8 GB RAM." This describes a:
questions.explanation: A guaranteed minimum amount of a resource is a reservation.

questions.question: Which statement about jumbo frames is WRONG?

options.A: They are larger than the standard 1500-byte frame
options.B: They reduce the number of frames needed for large transfers
options.C: They are smaller than standard frames

questions.explanation: Jumbo frames are larger, not smaller, than standard frames, so this statement is wrong.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.A: Caching keeps frequently used data in fast storage, and deduplication removes duplicate copies; both reduce disk I/O overhead
options.C: Deduplication keeps hot data in memory

questions.explanation: Caching keeps frequently used data in fast storage and deduplication removes duplicate copies, and both reduce disk I/O overhead.

questions.question: Why can stale snapshots also be a security problem?

options.B: They may hold outdated and unpatched data

questions.explanation: Old snapshots may hold outdated and unpatched data.

questions.question: What is the main difference between load balancing and high availability?

options.B: Load balancing aims for no downtime; HA aims for even load
options.C: Load balancing aims at performance by spreading work; HA aims at minimum downtime after failure

questions.explanation: Load balancing spreads work to improve performance, while HA aims at minimum downtime after a failure.

questions.question: Host A fails at night and its VMs restart automatically on Host B. Which feature made this possible?
questions.explanation: HA with clustered hosts restarts the VMs of a failed host on a healthy host automatically.

questions.question: Which technique mainly protects against site failure or disaster?
questions.explanation: Replication keeps a copy at another site, protecting against site failure or disaster.

questions.question: What is the relationship between DRS and vMotion?

options.A: DRS decides and balances load, using vMotion to move running VMs
options.C: DRS is a hypervisor, vMotion is a firewall

questions.explanation: DRS decides and balances load, and it uses vMotion to move running VMs between hosts.

questions.question: Which platform supports both para-virtualization and full virtualization?
questions.explanation: Xen supports both para-virtualization and full virtualization.

questions.question: Which platform has Medium scalability and a Limited ecosystem in the comparison table?
questions.explanation: In the comparison table, Microsoft Hyper-V has Medium scalability and a Limited ecosystem.

questions.question: Which row of the comparison table is correct?

options.D: Xen – Included in Windows Server – SCVMM – Not supported

questions.explanation: VMware vSphere is commercial, managed with vCenter and uses vMotion; the other rows contain wrong details.

questions.question: Which management pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Xen is managed with XenCenter, not Cockpit, so this pairing is incorrect.

questions.question: Which platform is described as purely commercial?
questions.explanation: VMware vSphere is the purely commercial platform; KVM and Xen are open-source and Hyper-V is included in Windows Server.

questions.question: What does VMware NSX integrated with vSphere provide?
questions.explanation: NSX integrated with vSphere provides virtual networks, micro-segmentation and firewalling.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence for the Hyper-V lab?

options.A: Test migration → create VMs → install role
options.B: Set up Hyper-V role → create VMs and virtual switches → test live migration and replication
options.C: Test replication → set up role → delete VMs

questions.explanation: The lab sets up the Hyper-V role first, then creates VMs and virtual switches, then tests live migration and replication.

questions.question: Which is NOT a step of Hyper-V replication setup?

options.A: Enable the replica server to receive replication
options.B: Select the VM and choose Enable Replication
options.D: Delete the primary VM before replication starts

questions.explanation: Deleting the primary VM is not a replication step, because the VM must exist to be replicated.

questions.question: Which action reduces the risk of over-commitment?

options.A: Allocating even more memory to all VMs
options.C: Using reservations for critical VMs and monitoring usage

questions.explanation: Reservations guarantee resources for critical VMs, and monitoring catches problems early.

questions.question: A suspicious file is opened inside a special VM so the main system stays safe. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Running something suspicious in a restricted, isolated VM to protect the main system is sandboxing.

questions.question: Right-sizing is important because:

options.A: It gives every VM the maximum resources
options.B: It avoids both over-provisioning (waste) and under-provisioning (slowness)

questions.explanation: Right-sizing avoids both waste from over-provisioning and slowness from under-provisioning.

questions.question: Which of the following are hypervisor-level metrics?

options.C: Scheduler latency, VM swap activity and resource contention

questions.explanation: Scheduler latency, VM swap activity and resource contention are hypervisor-level metrics.

questions.question: Periodic auditing also improves security because:

options.D: Forgotten VMs that may be unpatched are found and removed

questions.explanation: Auditing finds forgotten VMs that may be unpatched, so they can be removed.

questions.question: Network bandwidth monitoring may also reveal:

options.A: Unusual traffic that may be a security attack

questions.explanation: Monitoring bandwidth can reveal unusual traffic that may be a security attack.

questions.question: Encryption of data at rest helps because:

options.A: Stolen disks and backups cannot be read without the key
options.D: It removes the need for passwords

questions.explanation: Encrypted data at rest cannot be read from stolen disks or backups without the key.

questions.question: Why is logging especially useful in dynamic environments?

options.B: Logs help to keep track of VMs that move and change often

questions.explanation: Logs help keep track of VMs that move and change often.

questions.question: Which statement about vCenter is correct?

options.A: It is a hypervisor installed on each VM
options.D: It manages many ESXi hosts and enables features such as vMotion, DRS and HA

questions.explanation: vCenter manages many ESXi hosts and enables features such as vMotion, DRS and HA.

questions.question: Which statement about Hyper-V versus vSphere is correct?

options.A: Hyper-V is commercial and vSphere is free
options.B: Hyper-V is included in Windows Server and integrates with Azure
options.C: Hyper-V has the more advanced ecosystem

questions.explanation: Hyper-V is included in Windows Server and integrates with Azure.

questions.question: KVM is commonly managed with:
questions.explanation: KVM is commonly managed with tools such as virt-manager and Cockpit.

questions.question: Which statement about live migration across platforms is correct?

options.C: All four platforms support it, but names and tools differ
options.D: None of the platforms support it

questions.explanation: All four platforms support live migration, but the names and tools differ.

questions.question: In the memory trick H-V-I-S-D-D-I (security challenges), what does "S" stand for?
